The `engine` and `backend` arguments make different choices. The engine sets
the model runtime; the backend selects an implementation only within sparse
execution. The legacy engine remains the default. Within sparse execution,
`Matrix` is the supported general-purpose backend and the default backend.

This article uses the package's generated three-region fixture, so it can be
built without external model or data files.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE
)
helperPath = if (file.exists("helpers.R")) {
  "helpers.R"
} else {
  file.path("vignettes", "helpers.R")
}
source(helperPath, local = knitr::knit_global())
fixture = makeFirstSimulationFixture()
```

## Select the runtime and backend explicitly

Select `engine = "sparse"` when loading data and solving. Then request the
supported Matrix backend by its public identifier:

```{r matrix-backend}
model = GEModelR::GEModel$new()
model$loadTablo(fixture$tabloPath)
model$setClosure("tax")
model$loadData(fixture$inputData, engine = "sparse")
model$setShocks(setNames(4, 'tax["south"]'))
model$solveModel(
  iter = 1,
  steps = 1,
  engine = "sparse",
  backend = "Matrix",
  postsim = FALSE,
  diagnostics = TRUE
)
model$lastDiagnostics[c("engine", "requested_backend", "implementation", "status")]
```

The legacy engine is a separate runtime choice, not a sparse backend. Changing
`engine` requires loading the data again for that runtime. See the
```{r package-help-link, results='asis', echo=FALSE}
# pkgdown sets IN_PKGDOWN while rendering articles.
helpPage = if (identical(Sys.getenv("IN_PKGDOWN"), "true")) {
  "../reference/GEModelR-package.html"
} else {
  "../html/GEModelR-package.html"
}
cat(sprintf("[GEModelR package help](%s)", helpPage))
```
for the complete public method and output contract.

## Capability checks fail closed

Backend identifiers are requests, not hints. GEModelR checks whether the
requested implementation can run before dispatch. If a capability is missing
or the model is outside a structured backend's supported layout, the solve
reports a capability failure; it does not silently substitute another
backend.

`SuiteSparse` is recognized but unavailable in supported installed builds
pending portable support. Installing system libraries or setting its reserved
ordering option does not enable it. Select `backend = "Matrix"` for the
supported general sparse path. Structured and native backends also have
explicit capability requirements, such as a supported model layout and, for a
native implementation, compatible compiled symbols, ABI, Matrix factors, and
thread capabilities. An unavailable request fails preflight rather than
falling back to Matrix.

The following illustrates an unavailable request only; it is deliberately not
run as part of the vignette:

```{r unavailable-backend, eval=FALSE}
model$solveModel(engine = "sparse", backend = "SuiteSparse")
```

For package-name, option, and saved-state replacements from `tabloToR`, use the
[local migration guide](legacy-to-sparse.html) and the authoritative
`MIGRATION.md` in the source checkout. The canonical repository's first source
publication and hosted documentation are pending. Backend selection does not
change that package identity migration.
